common_name: Angelly Witch Hazel (Compact Pale Yellow AGM Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; Angelly stays noticeably more compact and upright than sprawling intermedia cultivars, making it a better fit for smaller shaded gardens.

directions: Angelly holds its pale, clear primrose-yellow, ribbon-petaled flowers in dense axillary clusters along bare stems from mid to late winter, giving a lighter, softer effect than the deep golds and coppers of many intermedia cultivars. It has earned the RHS Award of Garden Merit for its reliable floriferousness and unusually tidy, upright, compact habit compared with the wide-spreading growth typical of the group. Fall foliage turns respectable yellow-orange before dropping to expose the following winter's flower buds. Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade to full sun, and prune only lightly right after flowering.

common_name: Barmstedt Gold Witch Hazel (Deep Golden AGM Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Barmstedt Gold grows into a large, wide shrub, so allow generous room when siting it near a path or window.

directions: Raised at a German nursery in the town of Barmstedt, this RHS Award of Garden Merit cultivar carries large, deep golden-yellow, crimped ribbon petals above a reddish calyx, clustered thickly along leafless branches from late January into March. It is fragrant on mild days and, like other intermedia cultivars, curls its petals shut to protect them during hard freezes before reopening. The shrub matures into a broad, upright, rounded specimen with dark green summer foliage that turns clear yellow in fall. Grow in organically rich, moist, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, and prune only to remove damaged wood right after bloom.

common_name: Robert Witch Hazel (Coppery-Orange AGM Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic to neutral soil in partial shade to full sun; a sheltered woodland-edge spot helps hold both flower quality and fragrance through cold snaps.

directions: Robert is a medium-sized, RHS Award of Garden Merit witch hazel bearing fragrant, coppery-orange flowers with narrow, shredded-looking petals in typical dense clusters on bare winter branches. It stays somewhat more restrained in eventual size than the largest intermedia cultivars, making it a workable choice where a smaller winter accent shrub is wanted near a path or window. Good autumn foliage color adds a secondary season of interest before the leaves drop to reveal the coming winter's flower buds. Grow in acid to neutral, well-drained soil in sun or partial shade, sheltered from harsh winter wind, and prune only lightly right after flowering.

common_name: Rubin Witch Hazel (Ruby-Red AGM Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Rubin is one of the deepest red-flowered witch hazels available and flowers most heavily with good winter sun exposure.

directions: Rubin is a vigorous, upright, rounded witch hazel selection carrying slightly fragrant, ruby-red, ribbon-petaled flowers in dense clusters from mid to late winter, among the darkest and most saturated red tones found in the intermedia group alongside cultivars like Diane. It has earned the RHS Award of Garden Merit for its strong bloom performance and reliable habit. Medium green summer foliage gives way to warm autumn tones before dropping to reveal the flower buds set for the following winter. Grow in average, medium-moisture, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade, and limit pruning to shaping right after flowering.

common_name: Spanish Spider Witch Hazel (Strawberry-Yellow Bicolor AGM Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acid to neutral soil in an open, sunny to lightly shaded spot away from exposed or windy sites; Spanish Spider grows quite wide, so give it plenty of room.

directions: Spanish Spider is an RHS Award of Garden Merit cultivar named for its unusually long, twisting, strawberry-yellow petals tinged with red at the base, giving each mid- to late-winter flower cluster a distinctly leggy, spider-like look unlike the shorter ribbon petals of most intermedia cultivars. Its eventual size runs larger and wider than average for the group, so it works best as a specimen with room to spread rather than a tight foundation planting. Autumn foliage turns attractive yellow tones before dropping to expose the bare, flower-studded winter branches. Grow in well-drained, humus-rich, acid to neutral soil in an open, sheltered site, and prune only lightly right after bloom.

common_name: White Cascade Pieris (Vigorous Long-Trussed White-Flowered Andromeda)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; White Cascade is a vigorous older selection that produces exceptionally long flower trusses, so give it more room than compact modern Pieris cultivars.

directions: White Cascade is a classic, vigorous-growing Pieris selection valued for its unusually long, densely packed racemes of pure white, urn-shaped flowers that spill downward in early spring like a frothing waterfall, more profuse and longer than the flower trusses of the species. Glossy dark green leaves emerge yellowish-bronze when young before maturing to deep green, giving good textural contrast against the winter and spring bloom. It grows into a taller, more upright shrub than many newer compact cultivars, so it suits a background or specimen role in the shaded border rather than a small foundation planting. Site in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic soil in partial shade, sheltered from cold, drying winter wind.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)

common_name: Firecrest Pieris (Bright Red New-Growth AGM Andromeda)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Firecrest holds its brightest red new growth color when sheltered from harsh midday sun and drying wind.

directions: Firecrest is an RHS Award of Garden Merit cultivar bred by Hillier Nurseries in England, prized for the vivid, glossy red color of its emerging young leaves, which contrasts sharply with the pure white, lily-of-the-valley-like flowers opening in spring. The bright red new growth gradually shifts through bronze tones before settling into the mature dark green typical of the species, extending seasonal interest well past the bloom period. It grows into a dense, rounded evergreen shrub of moderate size, well suited to a shaded foundation planting or shrub border alongside other red-flushed Pieris selections. Grow in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic soil sheltered from cold winter wind and harsh afternoon sun.

common_name: Valley Rose Pieris (Pastel Pink-Flowered Compact Andromeda)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade, with full sun tolerated in cooler climates; Valley Rose is a slow grower, gaining only a few inches a year, so give it a permanent spot rather than a spot needing quick fill-in.

directions: Selected at a Pacific Northwest research nursery for its unusual flower color and disease resistance, Valley Rose opens deep pink buds that expand into airy clusters of rose-pink, urn-shaped flowers edged in ivory, so profuse in March and April that they can nearly hide the foliage before fading toward white. Bronzy new growth follows the spring bloom and matures to a dark, glossy green. Its slow, compact growth habit makes it a good fit for smaller shaded beds where faster Pieris cultivars would quickly outgrow the space. Grow in well-drained, slightly acidic, organically enriched soil in partial shade, protected from harsh winter wind.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in full sun to partial shade; like Brouwer's Beauty, Karenoma is a floribunda-japonica hybrid bred for extra cold hardiness beyond straight Pieris japonica cultivars.

directions: Karenoma combines the upright, bright white flower trusses and superior winter hardiness of native Pieris floribunda with the heavier bloom and refined habit of Pieris japonica, opening soft pink-tinted buds that expand into full, dense clusters of white spring flowers. The compact, rounded shrub stays a manageable size for a foundation or border planting, and its hybrid vigor gives it better cold tolerance than most purely japonica cultivars, extending the usable range of andromeda-type shrubs into colder gardens. Grow in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, and prune only lightly after flowering since old wood carries next year's buds. Established plants need little more than routine watering during dry spells.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in sun to part shade; Prelude is a var. yakushimanum selection that stays under 2 ft tall, well suited to small beds or rock-garden-style plantings.

directions: Prelude is a dwarf selection from the compact yakushimanum strain of Pieris japonica, forming a tight, low mound of foliage that stays well under 2 ft tall while spreading somewhat wider. Pinkish new leaves mature to a dark, glossy green, and pendulous panicles of small, fragrant, pure white flowers open later in spring than most Pieris cultivars, remaining fresh and attractive for an extended period. Its diminutive size and tidy habit make it a good choice for foundation plantings, rock gardens, or the front of a shaded border where larger Pieris selections would overwhelm the space. Grow in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic soil, and shelter from harsh winter wind and afternoon sun.
